name: Irresistible
lede: Irresistible is a deep rose-crimson with a name that reads like a sales pitch; no book read uses it as a color, and its history is that of the shades around it.

notes.cite: ColorHub library (data/library.json): ISCC-NBS 1955 blocks 255 and 258, Maerz & Paul 1930 dates, Werner no. 92 (Lake Red, near-duplicate dE 1.8)
ColorHub archive field notes for Irresistible (n=6), 23,781 museum paintings as photographed; data/graph/fieldnotes/i.json

sections.title: A name without a story
sections.body: In the books read the word appears only as an ordinary adjective, as when Garfield says Perkin's new colors proved irresistible to fashionable Paris and London [1]. None of them uses it as a color name, and the origin of the name is undocumented [1].

sections.title: The shades around it
sections.body: The library places the swatch in ISCC-NBS blocks 255 and 258 with a long list of older names [2]. Those include Madder, first recorded around 1804 by Maerz and Paul, China Rose in 1925 and Casino Pink in 1928 [2]. It also sits within two units of Werner's Lake Red, a color Werner matched to the red tulip and to spinel [2]. The nearest everyday name is [[mulberry]], and the family cousins are [[irresistible]] and [[crimson]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only 6 of 23,781 museum paintings contain the swatch color, about 0.03 per cent, rarer than 77 per cent of our named colors [3]. In printed English the adjective peaks in the 1820s, which is the word, not the color [3].

origin.first_recorded: not recorded in the books read
